title: serve() returns Box<dyn Error>, which is not Send and cannot be tokio::spawned or wrapped in anyhow
description:
persona-grpc/src/server.rs:14-17: `pub async fn serve(socket_path: &Path, service: WorkloadApiService) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>`.

`Box<dyn Error>` has no `Send + Sync` bound, so the returned future is not `Send`. A caller cannot `tokio::spawn(serve(path, svc))` — the standard way to run a server task alongside a shutdown signal or a second listener — and cannot use `?` on it inside any function returning `anyhow::Error` or `Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>`, which is most async application code. The workaround at every call site is `.map_err(|e| anyhow!(e.to_string()))`, i.e. throwing the error away and keeping the string.

The error is also untyped, so a caller cannot distinguish the four distinct failures this function has — stale socket removal (server.rs:20), parent directory creation (server.rs:25), bind (server.rs:27, the one worth reporting specially since it means another daemon is running), chmod (server.rs:32) and transport failure (server.rs:41) — without matching on message text.

Minimum fix: `Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>`. Better at 0.1.0: a `#[non_exhaustive] ServeError` enum with those cases, since persona-grpc already depends on thiserror (persona-grpc/Cargo.toml) and every other crate in the workspace defines a local error enum.

Also undocumented on this public function: it never returns on success (it runs until the transport stops), and per its own doc comment it deletes any existing file at `socket_path` (server.rs:18-21) — a destructive side effect on a caller-supplied path that the signature does not hint at.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.35 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
